problems.title: Type of Triangle
problems.concept: CASE WHEN A+B<=C OR A+C<=B OR B+C<=A THEN 'Not A Triangle' ... END
problems.question: Write a query identifying the type of each record in the TRIANGLES table using its three side lengths. Output 'Equilateral', 'Isosceles', 'Scalene', or 'Not A Triangle'.
problems.schema: TRIANGLES (A INT, B INT, C INT)
problems.sample_output:
Equilateral
Isosceles
Scalene
Not A Triangle
problems.sql_solution:
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN A + B <= C OR A + C <= B OR B + C <= A THEN 'Not A Triangle'
    WHEN A = B AND B = C THEN 'Equilateral'
    WHEN A = B OR B = C OR A = C THEN 'Isosceles'
    ELSE 'Scalene'
  END AS Triangle_Type
FROM TRIANGLES;
problems.explanation: Check triangle inequality rule first (sum of any 2 sides > 3rd side). If false, it's 'Not A Triangle'. Then check side equality for Equilateral, Isosceles, or Scalene.

problems.title: Finding Updated Records
problems.concept: MAX(salary) GROUP BY id, first_name, last_name, department_id
problems.question: We have a table with employee details who received pay raises over time. Find the current salary of each employee assuming that salary increases with time.
problems.schema: ms_employee_salary (id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, salary INT, department_id INT)
problems.sql_solution:
SELECT 
  id, 
  first_name, 
  last_name, 
  department_id, 
  MAX(salary) AS current_salary
FROM ms_employee_salary
GROUP BY id, first_name, last_name, department_id
ORDER BY id ASC;
problems.explanation: Group by employee ID and personal details, then select MAX(salary) to fetch the latest salary for each employee.

problems.title: Salaries Differences
problems.concept: MAX(marketing_salary) - MAX(engineering_salary)
problems.question: Calculates the difference between the highest salaries found in the marketing and engineering departments. Output just the absolute difference.
problems.schema:
db_employee (id INT, first_name VARCHAR, department_id INT, salary INT)
db_dept (id INT, department VARCHAR)
problems.sql_solution:
SELECT 
  ABS(
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.department = 'marketing' THEN e.salary ELSE 0 END) -
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.department = 'engineering' THEN e.salary ELSE 0 END)
  ) AS salary_difference
FROM db_employee e
JOIN db_dept d ON e.department_id = d.id;
problems.explanation: Join employees with department table, compute max salary for marketing and engineering using conditional MAX(CASE WHEN ...), then find absolute difference.
